chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Creating an atmosphere: show tunes, emceeing and scat singing
summary: He built the room by playing show tunes, MCing and singing for the first time, and set aside weeknights for visiting musicians.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh sure. But that's how I got that job. So it was such a scuffle trying to find some place to play and I had this house on me, so I made up my mind that I was goin' to create an atmosphere, create a job for myself. So gradually the guys began to come around. I started playing all these show tunes and people liked my sound, you know what I mean. And I started MCin' and doin' a little sing-ing, scat singing, you know. And they liked that.
Had you sung at all before this?

This was it! (laughter) And then I decided that Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday would be for the guys, you know, when they come in I'd announce their names and make 'em feel comfortable, no matter what style they played, and if there was new-comers comin' up, I'd announce their names and if he's young like Lou Donaldson and Horace Silvers (sic), like Horace Silvers worked there with me for a while and, you know, Monk and everybody, like Bird was there all the time and Bill Holiday, she would come in with Louis McKay. We mentioned this before didn't we?
